research:
I've collected enough. This is the write-up, using only information dated on or before 2026-08-20.

## 1. Resolution source
- Resolution uses the first value Freddie Mac publishes in its PMMS release for the week ending 2026-09-10, which FRED carries as MORTGAGE30US. That release should come out Thursday 2026-09-10 at about noon ET. I could not load FRED directly because the proxy refused the connection, so the figures below come from Freddie Mac releases as reported by search results.
- 2026-08-20: the latest reading is 6.65%, down from 6.67% the week before. The 15-year was 5.95%. [Freddie Mac](https://freddiemac.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mortgage-rates-decline-second-consecutive-week)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. Three more weekly readings come out first (8/27, 9/3, 9/10), and the 9/10 reading is the one that counts.
- 2026-08-20: at 6.65%, the rate sits close to the middle of the question's 6.25 to 6.95 range.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-19: daily rate trackers were mixed. Mortgage Research Center had the 30-year at 6.714%, up on the day, and Zillow had it at about 6.55%, slightly up. One headline said rates were "surprisingly calm amid bond market volatility." [Fortune](https://fortune.com/article/current-mortgage-rates-08-19-2026/), [Norada](https://www.noradarealestate.com/blog/todays-mortgage-rates-august-19-2026-update/)
- About 2026-08-18: the 30-year Treasury yield was reportedly about 5.29% to 5.33%, which would be its highest since 2007. This comes from a low-quality aggregator and is unverified. [Octagon](https://www.octagonai.co/markets/financials/interest-rates/30y-us-treasury-yield-on-aug-31-2026.md)
- 2026-08-13: July CPI came in as expected. Market-implied odds of a September Fed rate *hike* fell from 48% to 40%, and markets still fully priced a hike before year-end. [WATC daily report](https://www.watc.wa.gov.au/media/ksjkguxg/13082026_daily-report.pdf)
- 2026-08-13: Freddie Mac's 30-year averaged 6.67%. [Nasdaq/Freddie Mac](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/mortgage-rates-average-667-2026-08-13)
- In general, the macro backdrop is a Fed under Chair Kevin Warsh leaning toward tightening, with long yields high. That pushes rates up.

## 4. Base rates
Recent weekly values of the 30-year (search summaries of Freddie Mac releases):
- 07-02: 6.43
- 07-09: 6.49
- 07-16: 6.55
- 07-23: 6.58
- 07-30: 6.66
- 08-06: 6.69
- 08-13: 6.67
- 08-20: 6.65

Sources: [Freddie Mac](https://freddiemac.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mortgage-rates-average-658), [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/30-year-mortgage-rate/news/569358)

- Trend: the rate climbed about 23 basis points (bp) in July, then held flat to slightly lower between 6.65% and 6.69% in August.
- Typical variation: the resolution week is 3 weeks after the latest reading. Historically, 3-week changes have a standard deviation of roughly 10 to 15bp, and moves of 20bp or more happen maybe 15 to 25% of the time. This is a general rough estimate from history, not computed from FRED, which I could not reach.
- The most recent 3-week change was 6.66 to 6.65, which is -1bp.
- 2025-09-11 (about a year ago): the rate was about 6.35%. This is from my memory, not verified.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market on the 9/10 weekly value specifically.
- Kalshi runs "How high will the 30-year mortgage rate get in 2026" contracts. In April snapshots, the 6.5% threshold traded at about 59 to 62¢, 6.6% at about 43¢ and 7.0% at about 17¢. These are old and the 6.6% level has already been passed. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/KXMORTGAGERATE-26DEC-T6.6)
- Kalshi's "any 2026 PMMS below 5.75%" contract was at about 9¢ in an 08-01 snapshot. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/will-any-2026-freddie-mac-primary-mortgage-market-kalshi-kxfm30ymtg-26dec31-t)
- I found no fresh MBA, Fannie Mae or NAR forecasts for September.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-08-27: next PMMS release.
- About 2026-08-27 to 08-29: Jackson Hole symposium, with a keynote from Fed Chair Warsh. This is the main risk of a hawkish surprise.
- About 2026-08-28: July PCE inflation.
- 2026-09-03: PMMS release.
- About 2026-09-04: August jobs report. This is likely the biggest single data release for the 10-year Treasury yield before resolution.
- 2026-09-10: the resolving PMMS release. The survey covers rate quotes gathered mostly Monday to Wednesday, so data released after 9/9 has little effect on it.
- August CPI comes out around 09-10 to 09-11, likely too late to matter. The September FOMC meeting (about 09-15/16) is after resolution, but the hike odds people expect for it will move yields beforehand.
- A useful rule of thumb: the PMMS rate moves roughly with the 10-year Treasury yield. Around 08-20 the 10-year was in the mid-4.6% range, a spread of about 2.0 percentage points (inferred from late-August reporting of about 4.65%).
